news.title: Pinoys sustain form, rip Macau
news.lede: DT·30 October 2026 · 1:28 AM PHT·2 MIN READ. NATHAN Caligdong connects a goal that lifted the Filipinos to a 2-0 win over Macdau in the preliminaries of the FIFA U15 World Cup and Festival in Baku, Azerbaijan. BAKU, Azerbaijan — The Philippine U15 Men’s National Football Team (PMNFT U15) notched their third straight win in the inaugural FIFA U15 World Cup and Festival, beating Macau, 2-0, to start the classification stage Tier D round of 32 at the Hovsan Competition Complex. The young Filipinos dominated offensively, dominating possession and mounting numerous attacks to the Macau goal.

news.title: FIFA’s Reported $5 Billion World Cup Windfall Raises Question of Who the Game Is For
news.lede: Home » FIFA’s Reported $5 Billion World Cup Windfall Raises Question of Who the Game Is For. FIFA reportedly generated approximately $5 billion from ticket sales and hospitality at the 2026 World Cup, an extraordinary financial windfall following a tournament in which the organization’s aggressive pricing strategy sparked widespread anger from supporters, regulatory scrutiny and even reported opposition from within its own ranks. The figure, reported Thursday by The Times, represents more than five times the $929 million generated from tickets and hospitality at the 2022 World Cup in Qatar. It also significantly exceeds FIFA’s own financial projections for the tournament.

news.title: FIFA U-17 Women’s World Cup: “I See Flamingos in the Final” – Abiola Backs Nigeria Against Venezuela, Hails SSA Adeboye’s Fatherly Support
news.lede: Eniola Abiola Atanda, Principal Assistant to the Senior Special Assistant to the President on Grassroots Sports Development, has tipped Nigeria’s Flamingos to reach the final of the 2026 FIFA U-17 Women’s World Cup, expressing confidence ahead of their quarter-final clash against Venezuela, Sports247.ng reports. Atanda, who watched Nigeria’s thrilling 2-1 victory over Mexico from the stands in Morocco, believes the youngsters possess the unity, determination and fighting spirit required to challenge for the trophy. news.title: FIFA Team to Visit Morocco for Inspection of Ongoing World Cup Preparations
news.lede: A FIFA team will conduct an inspection tour of the 2030 World Cup co-host countries, including Morocco, in November and December. A communiqué from FIFA said the delegation will meet with representatives of local, regional, and national authorities in the three countries and inspect candidate stadiums as part of the ongoing planning process. The FIFA delegation will visit several host cities in Morocco, including Agadir, Fez, Marrakech, Rabat, and Tangier, as well as Casablanca. It will also visit host cities in Spain, including Bilbao, Barcelona, Las Palmas, Seville, Zaragoza, and San Sebastián.
